lines.sm1: A language model does not pick one word. It scores every possible next word, and turns the scores into probabilities.
lines.sm2: Then it samples: a random draw, weighted by those probabilities.
lines.tp1: Temperature reshapes the probabilities. A low temperature sharpens them, so the top word almost always wins.
lines.tp2: A high temperature flattens them, so unlikely words get a real chance.
lines.ef1: Run the same prompt several times. At low temperature, the answers are nearly identical.
lines.ef2: At high temperature they vary a lot, more creative, but also more likely to wander off.
lines.outro: Low temperature for facts and code. Higher temperature for brainstorming and stories. It is one dial, between reliable and creative.
